entities.name: Theodorus Priscianus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Theodorus Priscianus (born unknown, died 400 CE) was a physician at Constantinople during the fourth century.

He authored the Latin work Rerum Medicarum in four books, which remains a valuable source of medical knowledge from the late Roman Empire.

The work's significance extends beyond its medical content, as it provides insight into the cultural and intellectual context of late antiquity.

Priscianus's contributions to the field of medicine are still studied and referenced today, a testament to his enduring impact on the development of medical science.

His work also sheds light on the social and economic factors that influenced the growth and decline of the Roman Empire.

The legacy of Theodorus Priscianus serves as a reminder of the importance of preserving and studying historical medical texts, ensuring that the knowledge and expertise of the past continue to inform and shape our understanding of the present.

In the words of Priscianus himself, 'Medicina est scientia salutis et sanationis corporis' (Medicine is the science of health and the healing of the body).
